points: Yechezkel is lifted by a ruach and hears "Baruch kevod Hashem mimkomo." He is sent to the exiles at Tel Aviv in Bavel.
Tel Aviv means ruins and spring: old and new. Herzl's book "Altneuland" (Old-New Land) was translated into Hebrew as "Tel Aviv," and the city was named for it.
Hashem tells him: your job is to warn them, whether they listen or not. Rebuke is also so we don't become desensitized to what we see.
He is told to shut himself in his house and stay silent. Rashi: the people are no longer worthy of rebuke. Many traditions say it lasted seven years, and leaders came to learn from him there.
"Baruch kevod Hashem mimkomo": even when Hashem seems far, His blessing is heard right where we are. In Kedushah, "Kadosh" (He fills the world) and "mimkomo" (we can't fully reach Him) go together.
